title: Through Sorrow's Night and Danger's Way
description: Through Sorrow's Night and Danger's Way in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Henry Kirke White wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 360 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Christian's Contest, Rest, and Hope”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Through sor-row's night and dan-ger's way A-mid the deep-ening gloom, The sol-diers of an in-jured King Are march-ing to the tomb.

lines: Through sorrow's night and danger's way
The soldiers of an injured King
The storms of life shall beat.
Yet not thus lifeless in the grave
O'er nature's ruins it shall rise,
Then heaven's soft dew o'er every eye
And the long silent dust shall wake

licence: Public domain: Henry Kirke White died in 1806.
credits: Words by Henry Kirke White (1785–1806), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
